It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the former {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=shrine ranking system}} its rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. Its shrine crest is the "mokkō". {{nihongo|'''Umajiisobe Shrine'''|馬路石邊神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

== History ==
It is said to have been founded in {{ill|Hakuhō|Q11580612|qid=Q11580612}} 3 ({{ill|663|ab|663|af|663|als|663|am|663 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|663|ar|663|ary|663|ast|663|az|663|azb|۶۶۳ (میلادی)|be|663|be_x_old|663|bg|663|bn|৬৬৩|bpy|মারি ৬৬৩|br|663|bs|663.|ca|663|cdo|663 nièng|ceb|663|ckb|٦٦٣|crh|663|cs|663|cv|663|cy|663|da|663|de|663|el|663|eml|663|eo|663|es|663|et|663|eu|663|fa|۶۶۳ (میلادی)|fi|663|fo|663|fr|663|fy|663|ga|663|gan|663年|gd|663|gl|663|he|663|hi|663|ht|663 (almanak jilyen)|hu|663|hy|663|id|663|io|663|it|663|ja|663年|jv|663|ka|663|kk|663 жыл|ko|663년|la|663|lb|663|lij|663|lmo|663|lt|663 m.|map_bms|663|mdf|663|mg|663|mhr|663|mk|663|mr|इ.स. ६६३|mrj|663 и|ms|663|mzn|۶۶۳|nah|663|nap|663|nds|663|nds_nl|663|new|सन् ६६३|nl|663|nn|663|no|663|nrm|663|nso|663|oc|663|or|୬୬୩|os|663-æм аз|pl|663|pnb|663|pt|663|qu|663|ro|663|ru|663 год|rue|663|sa|६६३|scn|663|sd|663ع|se|663|sh|663.|shn|663|si|663|sk|663|sl|663|sq|663|sr|663|su|663|sv|663|sw|663|tg|Соли 663|th|พ.ศ. 1206|tk|663|tl|663|tly|663|tr|663|tt|663 ел|uk|663|ur|663ء|uz|663|vec|663|vi|663|war|663|wuu|663年|xmf|663|zh|663年|zh_min_nan|663 nî|zh_yue|663年|qid=Q31122}}), during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|qid=Q335181}}, and that in {{ill|Shuchō|de|Shuchō|es|Shuchō|fa|شوچو (دوره آسوکا)|fr|Ère Shuchō|hr|Shuchō|ia|Shucho|id|Shuchō|ja|朱鳥|ko|슈초|ru|Сютё|simple|Shuchō|sr|Шучо|th|ชูโจ|tr|Shuchō|uk|Сютьо|zh|朱鸟|zh_yue|朱鳥|qid=Q777413}} 1 ({{ill|686|Q30619|qid=Q30619}}) Ōanamuji-no-Mikoto was {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|Q11412524|qid=Q11412524}}. In ancient times, it was worshipped as the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} by the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Isobe-no-Kimi}} family, a {{ill|Gōzoku|Q84066|qid=Q84066}} based in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Umaji-gō}}.

In the mid-{{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} lists it as "Umajiisobe Shrine, Yasu District, {{ill|Ōmi Province|Q843882|qid=Q843882}}," placing it among shikinaisha. In the medieval period, as the {{ill|Chinjusha|Q13479654|qid=Q13479654}} of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tanaka-no-shō}}, it was called "Tanaka Daimyōjin" and "Tanaka Tennō-sha."

In the Sengoku period, it was revered by the {{ill|Rokkaku clan|Q2975342|qid=Q2975342}}, but shrine buildings were lost in the conflicts of {{ill|Genki (era)|Q1145064|qid=Q1145064}} and {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}}. It was rebuilt in the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, and the current buildings date to {{ill|Bunkyū|Q730266|qid=Q730266}} 2 ({{ill|1862|Q7698|qid=Q7698}}).

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 9 ({{ill|1876|Q7766|qid=Q7766}}), it was ranked village shrine in the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, and in Meiji 14 it was promoted to {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

== Precincts ==

ファイル:馬路石邊神社 拝殿.JPG|'''Haiden'''

The current shrine buildings were constructed in {{ill|Bunkyū|Q730266|qid=Q730266}} 2 ({{ill|1862|Q7698|qid=Q7698}}).

Along the approach stands a "Mikoshi-zuka" mound said to contain a buried mikoshi.
